problem: Floorplan extraction methods (HEAT, RoomFormer) ignore room semantics and break on real, noisy, cluttered scans with curved walls. 3D open-vocabulary segmentation (OpenScene, OpenMask3D) works at object or point level and cannot segment or label whole regions like 'kitchen'.
motivation: Navigation and planning need a hierarchical understanding of a scene (objects, rooms, room-to-room connections) that can be queried in free-form language. Top-down density maps are sensitive to scan quality and cannot separate open doorways from walls or closed doors. Room type can be inferred from the objects a room contains.
key_idea: Segment rooms and doorways with Mask R-CNN on a 3-channel map (density plus floor-slice and ceiling-slice occupancy), then use a self-attention transformer over the CLIP embeddings of the objects in each room to produce room embeddings aligned to CLIP text, which makes room-level language queries possible.
insight: The floor and ceiling occupancy slices expose open doorways as the difference between the two slices. Ablation (single vs multi channel): Matterport3D room AP 84.83 -> 88.47 and transition AP 50.47 -> 60.92. Attention over object CLIP embeddings beats simple averaging (F1 60.94 vs 75.43), and the contrastive text-aligned head is slightly better than a logits head (F1 75.43 vs 74.63) while also keeping the embedding queryable. Even the single-channel Mask R-CNN beats the polygon-fitting baselines on Matterport3D, so the instance-mask formulation itself helps on real data.
method: Multi-channel occupancy input: stacks the top-down density map D with binary occupancy slices at floor height (0.1h-0.3h) and ceiling height (0.7h-0.9h), on the same grid resolution.
Room/transition segmentation: Mask R-CNN (ResNet50 backbone, anchors 32-256, NMS 0.5, AdamW lr 2e-4) as a 3-class instance segmentation task (room, transition, background).
3D object map: ConceptGraphs pipeline (SAM masks, CLIP crop features, multi-view fusion) from posed RGB-D gives object point clouds with 1024-d CLIP embeddings.
Object-to-room association: room masks are mapped back to world coordinates; each object's centroid is assigned to the room via a KD-tree nearest match.

Room labeling transformer: an 8-layer, 8-head, 1024-d encoder takes [CLS; object CLIP features]; the CLS output is the room embedding, trained with an NT-Xent-style contrastive loss (tau 0.5) against CLIP text embeddings of room labels (400 epochs, lr 1e-5, dropout 0.2).

Inference and querying: the label is the argmax cosine similarity between the CLS embedding and room-name text embeddings; natural-language queries (e.g. 'place to cook') are matched against room embeddings.

setting.backbone: Mask R-CNN (ResNet50) for rooms/doors; CLIP + SAM (ConceptGraphs) for object features; 8-layer self-attention transformer for room labels (trained)
setting.training_data: Structured3D (3000 train / 250 val / 250 test) and Matterport3D (80% train / 20% test) with the authors' manual doorway annotations; no extra web data beyond pretrained CLIP/SAM
setting.observation: 3D point cloud from posed RGB-D sequences (offline), converted to top-down density and occupancy maps; object CLIP embeddings
setting.action_space: none (scene understanding, not an embodied agent)
setting.privileged: Room-labeling baseline comparison uses ground-truth object-to-room association for all methods; the full pipeline uses predicted room masks

results: Room segmentation AP rises to 98.86 on Structured3D (vs RoomFormer 96.93) and 88.47 on Matterport3D (vs RoomFormer 64.42), and doorway AP to 60.92 (vs 24.85). Room labeling F1 is 75.43 vs 62.75 for the strongest baseline (embedding-based). The complete pipeline gets 74.02 mAP@0.5 vs 23.52 for RoomFormer.
limitations: Rooms not visible top-down (noise or very small size) are missed, and rooms with no detected objects cannot get an embedding.
Relies on walls, so it cannot split open-plan spaces into sub-room 'zones'.
Offline only, with no navigation evaluation; depends on ConceptGraphs object maps and needs a 2D-projection assumption.
